extracted.intended_audience: researchers and engineers working on scientific-retraction studies, dataset creators, and developers of automated verification / NLP systems (e.g., arXiv/ML/NLP researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and releasing a large-scale dataset of withdrawn/withdrawn-version arXiv papers and categorizing withdrawal reasons; includes harvesting IDs, extracting and anonymizing comments, clustering/labeling, zero-shot categorization, evaluation, and responsible data-release controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual/methodological/other critical errors in manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: This category encompasses retractions due to significant mistakes in the research process or results. These errors could range from flawed experimental designs to incorrect data analysis to proof/lemma errors, potentially invalidating the study’s conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “The paper is withdrawn due to a fatal mistake on pp. 7. The author is now satisfied to see that the integral of (14) actually converges in the limit x -> 1/2, as opposed to the claim of the paper in pp. 7.” Includes anything from small technical mistakes to fundamental flaws that invalidate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete exposition or more work in progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may retract articles that they deem incomplete or requiring substantial additional work. This often occurs when researchers realize their initial submission was premature and requires further development or refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “Withdrawn due to the fact that [the] proposed approach is restricted to discrete chiral symmetry and not easily generalizable to continuous chiral symmetry.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Typos in manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Retractions due to typographical errors that can alter the meaning of critical information or data in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: corrections to math notation that materially change expressions: the manuscript used \mathbb{R}\%_{+}^{n} instead of \mathbb{R}_{+}^{n}. Even apparent 'minor' typos can necessitate withdrawal if they affect correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-identified as “not novel”
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers withdraw their work upon realizing their findings or ideas have already been published or are not as original as initially thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “This paper has been withdrawn by the author because it is a corollary of a well-known result by Monsky.” Used to preserve integrity and avoid presenting non-original contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative or legal issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Retractions due to non-scientific reasons such as authorship disputes, copyright infringements, or institutional/third-party authorization issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “The paper has been withdrawn waiting for the authorization from APS to reproduce two pictures published in Phys.Rev.B 63,045202 (2001).”

rubrics_metrics.name: ArXiv policy violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles removed because they do not adhere to arXiv’s submission guidelines or ethical standards (administrative removals by arXiv admins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example arXiv admin note: “This submission has been removed by arXiv administrators due to unprofessional personal attack.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsumed by another publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An arXiv preprint withdrawn because its content has been incorporated into another paper or publication (to avoid duplication/self-plagiarism/salami-slicing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “Most of the (correct) portion of this paper has been incorporated into the paper ‘On the Markoff equation’ (arXiv:1208.4032).”

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Retractions involving copying significant portions of others' work without proper attribution — serious breaches of academic ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “withdrawn by arXiv administrators due to excessive unattributed and verbatim text overlap with the pre-existing Wikipedia article on redshift.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawals driven by personal circumstances unrelated to the scholarly quality (e.g., coauthor disagreements, embarrassment, private matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “This version was posted without enough prior discussion with my collaborator. My collaborator would prefer it not to be posted at this time.” These often have explicit first-person language and may be sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason not specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawals where authors or arXiv administrators do not provide a clear explanation for the withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “The authors have decided to withdraw this submission. Clarifications/corrections, if any, may follow at a later date.” May reflect privacy choices or undisclosed factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy of retraction reasons (10-category schema)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset's canonical taxonomy: (1) Factual/methodological/other critical errors in manuscript; (2) Incomplete exposition or more work in progress; (3) Typos in manuscript; (4) Self-identified as ‘not novel’; (5) Administrative or legal issues; (6) ArXiv policy violation; (7) Subsumed by another publication; (8) Plagiarism; (9) Personal reasons; (10) Reason not specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The taxonomy was derived by embedding comments, K-means clustering (K=100), and manual review. Detailed explanations and examples for each category are provided in the paper (Section 5). Use this schema for classification/analysis of withdrawn arXiv comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment clustering / category discovery procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed withdrawal comments with an off‑the‑shelf text embedding model and cluster embeddings using K-means with a large K (K=100), then manually review clusters to identify categories and hard test cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach aims to capture nuance by overclustering and manual consolidation; produces the 10-category taxonomy. Guidance: generate many clusters to avoid missing rare patterns; manually label clusters and identify hard cases for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment extraction and PII scrubbing
rubrics_metrics.description: Crawl arXiv abstract pages to extract comment sections, subject areas, and version URLs; before further processing, scrub the dataset of any personally identifiable information (PII).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation detail: use tools like scrubadubdub (NLP-based) to replace PII with placeholders like [RETRACTED_NAME] and [RETRACTED_EMAIL]. PII is rare but must be removed prior to release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harvesting withdrawn arXiv identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain all withdrawn article IDs from arXiv (the authors worked with arXiv to collect IDs as of a cutoff date). Note: withdrawn IDs may include multiple withdrawn versions of the same article (e.g., v3 and v5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: working with arXiv avoids filtering entire dumps; resulting list in this work had 16,460 article-version entries; anticipate ~11% representing different versions of the same article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-shot comment categorization prompt spec
rubrics_metrics.description: A zero-shot GPT-4 prompt: classify a withdrawal comment into one of the 10 categories and return JSON {"category": <category>}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact instruction used: provide the comment and the list of categories; require JSON output. Test with hard cases (samples included). Example mappings: “This paper has been withdrawn by the author. Please see arXiv:0806.0780” -> Subsumed by another publication; “the data set did not pass the IRB review” -> Administrative or legal issues; “60F15” -> Reason not specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sampling protocol for human annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Manually annotate a stratified sample for evaluation: choose 10% of the comments in each category or 50 if 10% < 50, or all if the category has < 50, yielding an annotation set for measuring classifier performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied here to produce 1,620 hand-labeled comments. Guidance: stratify by category to ensure adequate representation of rarer classes for reliable per-category metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance metrics and reporting (per-category and weighted F1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate classifier performance with per-category F1-scores and a weighted average F1-score to summarize overall effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this work, per-category F1 scores ranged from 0.7013 to 1.0 and the weighted average F1 was 0.9594. Report confusion matrices and per-class metrics to diagnose confusions (e.g., 'not novel' confused with 'subsumed by another publication').

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-in-the-loop hard-case identification and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify hard cases during manual cluster review and include them as test cases to validate prompting and classification robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a curated set of challenging examples during prompt tuning/testing to ensure edge cases are handled; authors tested hard cases and verified they passed before large-scale deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: WithdrarXiv-SciFy enriched subset for feasibility studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Release an enriched subset of the dataset including scripts to produce parsed full-text PDFs, intended to enable research in scientific feasibility studies, claim verification, and automated theorem proving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the enriched subset for downstream tasks (e.g., parsed full text for SciFy research). Provide scripts and parsed artifacts to facilitate experiments in proof checking, claim verification, and figure/text discrepancy detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Themes within 'Factual/methodological/other critical errors' (8 sub-themes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight major themes found by clustering comments in the largest withdrawal category: (1) Errors in Proofs, (2) Misconceptions in Theoretical Foundations, (3) Issues in Experiment Design or Data Analysis, (4) Calculation and Numerical Errors, (5) Gaps in Mathematical Arguments, (6) Flawed Methodologies, (7) Incorrect Assumptions or Misinterpretations, (8) Errors in Figures or Visual Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each theme is illustrated by example phrases (e.g., “error in the proof of the main theorem”, “gap in the proof”, “error in experimental results”, “wrong figures”). These themes can inform automated detectors or feature design for verification systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible dataset-release controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Four concrete steps employed to protect authors and responsibly release the dataset: (1) exclude rows categorized as 'personal reasons'; (2) scrub all PII from extracted comments; (3) release via HuggingFace gated access; (4) implement a 'right to be forgotten' process allowing authors to request exclusion of specific arXiv IDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: withdrawals can divulge sensitive or embarrassing information even if public; use high-accuracy filters (near-perfect detection of 'personal reasons' reported) plus technical and policy controls to balance openness and author/privacy protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of off-the-shelf embedding and clustering pipeline with manual review
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine automated embedding+clustering with human validation to derive interpretable categories rather than fully automated labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice: embed comments (Nussbaum et al. embedder), K-means K=100, then manual cluster inspection and labeling. This hybrid pipeline balances scalability with accuracy and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting distributional insights and subject-area normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting counts of retraction reasons by subject area, account for differing base rates (absolute counts vs retraction rates) to avoid misleading conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: AI topics (cs.CV, cs.LG) have highest absolute retraction counts but some math subfields (math.CO, math.DG) show higher relative retraction rates; when cross-listing occurs count in each applicable category but present retraction rates alongside counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical consideration: sensitivity of aggregated withdrawal comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregated withdrawal comments can surface sensitive details at scale; exercise caution in handling, disseminating, and enabling downstream use of such aggregated data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though comments are public and under CC, aggregation and easy searching increase risk. Use exclusion, PII scrubbing, gated access, and right-to-be-forgotten to mitigate harms.
